Experimental. A VyOS router's host name. Removing this step leaves the name as it is.

**Experimental.** Network devices are new, and this module may change between releases. It's tested against VyOS 2026.11.13-0016-rolling in a container on a lab VM, not yet in CI.

Use `vyos_hostname` to name a VyOS router. The change goes in like every VyOS step does: a dry run, `commit-confirm`, then a confirm and save over a new login, once per router per circuit. See [`vyos_config`](/modules/vyos_config).

## Example usage

```hcl
step "name" {
  vyos_hostname {
    name = each.key
  }
}
```

## Arguments

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes | Host name, such as r1. VyOS takes letters, digits and hyphens. |

## Read-only attributes

Conn3x sets these; reference them as `conn3x_vyos_hostname.<circuit>__<step>["<host>"].<name>`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `in_sync` | bool | Whether the router had this name at the last refresh. |
| `revision` | string | Changes each time Conn3x changes this on the host. Handlers watch it. |

A step lowers to the `conn3x_vyos_hostname` resource, one instance per host, and connects with its circuit's `ssh` block.
